content:
ashok: Quick sync — following up on the RFC for a unified ingress rate stack (edge leaky-buckets + local provisional admit). I sketched two deployment options, want quick thumbs and objections before I turn this into a concrete playbook. link: https://r.rw/r/unified-ingress-rfc

maria: looked at the sketch this morning. main worry is cross-tenant fairness when we move more admission logic to edge proxies. how do we prevent one noisy tenant from starving others if the proxy has stale view?

ashok: good question. Option A keeps a lightweight fairness shard at the central controller that issues short-lived reservations (1–5s). Proxies do local leaky-bucket admission based on those reservations. Option B pushes more heuristics into proxies and only reports telemetry to controller (no reservations). A trades complexity for stronger fairness. B trades fairness for lower control-plane ops.

liam: from perf side, Option A adds ~1 RPC per reservation. we can batch reservations per proxy every 100ms to amortize. needs benching.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster "ingress-proxy-canary-3" updated with reservation-client v0.3.2

ashok: rough config I proposed for Option A (how proxies consume reservations):
```yaml
proxy: 
  reservation_window_ms: 1000
  reservation_batch_ms: 100
  fallback_strategy: local-leaky-bucket
  soft_watermarks: [0.6, 0.9] # scale degrade points
```

maria: +1 to soft watermark idea. Also need clear signal for abuse vs legitimate burst so we don't auto-penalize customers during traffic spikes (marketing campaigns etc). can we add an exemption token for verified critical tenants?

ashok: yes — proposal includes an "escrow" flag attached to reservations for VIP tenants. escrow reduces penalty multiplier and extends grace window. but that interacts with cost fairness — we need accounting to bill for reserved capacity.

tess: question: what changes to /admit API are required? Our current contract returns admit=true/false + tokens. If we add reservations, we need to return reservation_id and expiry. backwards compat: keep current fields and add optional reservation metadata. migration path: proxies can ignore reservation_id until they opt-in.

liam: telemetry checklist for rollout (promql examples):
- reservation_success_rate = sum(rate(reservation_grant_total[1m])) / sum(rate(reservation_request_total[1m]))
- proxy_local_drop_rate = sum(rate(proxy_drop_total[1m])) by (proxy) / sum(rate(proxy_in_requests_total[1m]))
- fairness_skew = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_use_bucket[5m])) by (tenant)) / avg_over_time(sum(rate(token_use[5m]))[30m:])

maria: agree on metrics. also need alert on reservation_staleness: count(reservation_expired_without_use) / grant_total > 0.05 over 5m. that indicates mismatch between controller and proxy clocks or batching windows.

ashok: rollout plan idea: 1) deploy reservation-capable proxies in canary (read-only), 2) enable reservations for internal tenants only, 3) enable per-region canary tenants, 4) open to all with billing tag. each step gated by success criteria above.

liam: perf experiments to run: synthetic tenants with 10k rps aggregate, 100 tenants, mix of bursty and steady. measure median p99 delta on admission path and reservation RPC latency. let's schedule a bench run this week.

ops-bot: bench-run scheduled: ingress-reservation-canary-2024-07-17 at 2024-07-17T21:00Z

maria: security note: reservation metadata must be signed by controller (HMAC) so proxies cannot be spoofed. plus TTL short enough to prevent replay (<=5s).

ashok: agreed. also need to store reservation audit trail for billing and postmortems. storage options: append-only reservation log vs event stream. prefer event stream into kafka topic "reservations.v1".

tess: interface change proposal (backwards compatible): add optional fields to /admit response: reservation_id, reservation_expires_at, escrow_flag, signature. proxies default to existing logic if reservation_* missing.

liam: minor: ensure proxies validate signature using rotating keys from KMS + JWK endpoint. add metrics for signature_validation_failures.

maria: last thought — fairness algorithm. controller should consider token-cost-per-request (model type) not just request counts. otherwise tenants using large-model calls will get starved. add weight parameters per model in reservation allocator.

ashok: yes — weight-aware allocator is in RFC v1.2. good catch. I'll update the playbook with (a) backcompat contract for /admit, (b) telemetry queries, (c) bench plan, (d) security HMAC details, (e) billing/escrow flow.

ashok: can everyone react with :thumbsup: if no blockers so I can open a follow-up PR?

maria: :thumbsup:

liam: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: ticket created: INFRA-4378 "ingress reservation rollout playbook" assigned to @ashok

ashok: thanks — I'll post the PR and schedule the bench. any late objections ping me directly.
